<symbol=case_file_head>Basic Rules

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>This game is played with a hanafuda deck.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Matching a card in your hand with one of the table allows you to take that card.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>The object of the game is to form special card combinations to outscore your opponents.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> There are twelve card suits consisting of the months of the year (January to December).
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Each suit consists of four cards.
28-1482:
<symbol=case_file_head>Basic Rules

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>When it's your turn, place one card from your hand on the table.

　　If there is another card of the same suit on the table: <symbol=case_file_right_arrow> You collect the pair.
　　If there are no other cards of the same type on the table: <symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Your card stays on the table.


　<symbol=case_file_subhead>When you form a specific combination with acquired cards, you can select whether to call "Koi" and keep going.

　　Call "Koi"　 <symbol=case_file_right_arrow> The hand continues and you try to form more combinations.
　　Don't Call "Koi" <symbol=case_file_right_arrow> The hand ends and you get the points for the card combinations you hold.

28-1498:
<symbol=case_file_head>Oicho-kabu Rules

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>This game is played with a hanafuda deck, but only the cards from January to October are used.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Each month has a numeric value equal to where it is on the calendar (e.g. January is 1 and October is 10).

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Players are each dealt two or three cards, which they then total up.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>For totals over 10, only the last digit (ones place) is used. The player closest to 9 wins.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>There are four players, including a dealer.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>The dealer plays against the other players, who place the bets.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>The dealer changes when a round ends.
28-1499:
<symbol=case_file_head>Oicho-kabu Rules

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Four cards are dealt face-up on the table.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Each player selects one card from the four on the table as the one to bet on.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Next, each player receives an additional card from the deck.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>The non-dealer players may stay with two cards or draw a third card to go into the showdown with a total of three cards.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Players who choose a third card may draw it from the deck at this time.
28-1500:
<symbol=case_file_head>Oicho-kabu Rules

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>The dealer draws once the three other players are staying.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>After drawing two cards, the dealer may choose to draw a third.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>The dealer may also choose which players to challenge with two cards and which to challenge with three.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Once the winners are decided and the points calculated, the dealer changes and the game proceeds to the next round.
28-1501:
<symbol=case_file_head>Score Calculation

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>A Four-One and a Nine-One each pay double your bet, while a three of a kind triples it.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>A Ten-Ten-One increases the pay by 20.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>For all other hands, the payout is the same as your bet.

<symbol=case_file_head>Texas Hold'em Rules

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Texas Hold'em is a poker game in which you build five-card hands from
　　seven cards (your own two hole cards, plus five community cards).


<symbol=case_file_lower_than>How to Win<symbol=case_file_greater_than>
　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Have the strongest hand at the showdown.
　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> All the other players fold.
28-1507:
<symbol=case_file_head>Flow of the Game

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>In the first round, each player is dealt two hole cards. Three community cards are dealt in the second round. The fourth and fifth
　　community cards are dealt in the third and fourth rounds, respectively.


　<symbol=case_file_lower_than>Advancing to the Next Round<symbol=case_file_greater_than>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>All players have placed bets of the same amount.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Once All Players Have Checked:


　<symbol=case_file_subhead>At the end of the fifth round, all players reveal their hands in a showdown. 
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>The player with the strongest hand wins.
28-1508:
<symbol=case_file_head>How a game of "Texas Hold'em" goes

　<symbol=case_file_lower_than>Possible Actions in Each Round<symbol=case_file_greater_than>

　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Bet: Bet a fixed amount of chips.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Call: Bet the same amount of chips as the previous player.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Raise: Bet more chips than the previous player.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Check: Don't bet, in which case the next player goes.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Fold: Stop betting and retire from the current hand.


　<symbol=case_file_subhead>You may place a bet if none of the other players have bet yet.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>You can check if none of the other players have bet yet, or if all the other players call the big blind.
28-1509:
<symbol=case_file_head>Flow of the Game

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>A big blind and little blind are forced bets at the beginning of a hand that must be made by the first and second players that
　　get the dealer button after the current dealer. (The dealer button rotates clockwise after each hand.)

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Bet Amounts Each Round
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Big Blind: Minimum bet
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Little Blind: Half the minimum bet

28-1522:
<symbol=case_file_head>Mahjong Rules

　<symbol=case_file_lower_than>Basic Rules<symbol=case_file_greater_than>

　　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Four players compete to be the first to complete a 14-tile hand.
　　<symbol=case_file_subhead>This hand is typically composed of 4 groups of 3-tile combinations and 1 pair.
　　<symbol=case_file_subhead>The point value of a player's hand is determined by the tiles they have collected.
　　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Each player takes turns drawing and discarding tiles to construct their hand to reach the win condition.
　　<symbol=case_file_subhead>In addition to drawing them, players can steal certain tiles that their opponents discard.
28-1523:
<symbol=case_file_subhead>As you play through a game, you will draw and discard tiles while trying to form sets of straights and three-of-a-kinds
　　　to meet the win condition.
　　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Sometimes you can steal from others players to reach that goal quicker.
　　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Aim to form 4 sets of 3 (straights or triplets) and 1 pair.

　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> A Shuntsu is 3 consecutive numbers of the same suit.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> A Kotsu is a set of 3 identical tiles.

　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Toitsu is a pair of 2 of the same tile.
28-1526:
<symbol=case_file_head>Melds


　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Immediately after an opponent discards a tile, you can claim and add it to your hand, creating a "meld."
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Melds are divided into pon, chi, and kan, explained on the next page.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>A concealed hand is when Pon, Chi, or Kan has not been declared.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> There are hands that can only be formed through a concealed hand.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Also, there are some hands that will have their scoring elements taken down if they have melded.
28-1527:
<symbol=case_file_head>Types of Melds

　<symbol=case_file_lower_than>Pon<symbol=case_file_greater_than>:
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>If an opponent discards a tile that matches a pair in your hand, that tile can be claimed and melded to form a triplet
　　by selecting "Pon."

　<symbol=case_file_lower_than>Chi<symbol=case_file_greater_than>:
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>If an opponent discards a tile that completes a 3-number straight, that tile can be claimed and melded to form a set by
　　selecting "Chi." You can only steal a tile from the opponent sitting to your left for this meld. 

　<symbol=case_file_lower_than>Kan<symbol=case_file_greater_than>:
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>If you have a triplet and an opponent discards a fourth matching tile, you can select "Kan" to claim it and form an exposed kan. 
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>If you have an exposed pon and draw the fourth tile, you may select "Kan" to upgrade that pon into a kan.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Each time a kan is announced, a new dora (bonus title) is added.
28-1528:
<symbol=case_file_head>Completing a Hand

　There are two ways to complete a hand: ron and tsumo.

　　<symbol=case_file_lower_than>Ron<symbol=case_file_greater_than> (completing a hand by stealing):
　　　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Any time you need one more tile to win, you can claim the current discard if it completes your hand by selecting "Ron."

　　<symbol=case_file_lower_than>Tsumo<symbol=case_file_greater_than> (completing a hand with a self-drawn tile):
　　　Any time you need one more tile to win and you draw a tile that completes your hand, you can select "Tsumo."


　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>When you win by ron, the opponent who discarded the winning tile pays you the resulting points.
　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>When you win by tsumo, your three opponents pay the resulting points.

　　　<symbol=case_file_lower_than><symbol=button_shikaku><symbol=button_shikaku>Reverse<symbol=button_sankaku><symbol=button_sankaku><symbol=case_file_greater_than>　Finisher Effect: Bind
　　　<symbol=case_file_lower_than><symbol=button_shikaku><symbol=button_shikaku><symbol=button_shikaku>Reverse<symbol=button_sankaku><symbol=button_sankaku><symbol=case_file_greater_than>
　　　<symbol=case_file_lower_than><symbol=button_shikaku><symbol=button_shikaku><symbol=button_shikaku><symbol=button_shikaku>Reverse<symbol=button_sankaku><symbol=button_sankaku><symbol=case_file_greater_than>

　　　While the enemy is knocked down or in the middle of getting back up, the Bind or Launch effects will not be triggered.
29-0025:
<symbol=case_file_head>Learn the Foundation of Defense
　　　<color=red>Guarding</color> is a crucial ability that allows you to block enemy attacks.
　　　<symbol=case_file_lower_than><symbol=button_l1><symbol=case_file_greater_than>

<symbol=case_file_head>Beware of Back Attacks
　　　You cannot guard against attacks that come from behind you.

<symbol=case_file_head>To avoid this, maintain a fighting stance with <symbol=button_r1> and try to keep your attacker
　　　in front of you.

<symbol=case_file_head>Beware of Blades and Bullets
　　　Some attacks can't be blocked with bare hands. In these situations, use <symbol=button_maru> 
　　　to pick something up and improvise it as a weapon. When you guard with a
　　　weapon in hand, you'll be able to protect against most dangerous attacks.
　　　
<symbol=case_file_head>Guards Can Be Broken
　　　Getting your guard broken will leave you wide open, but this can be
　　　mitigated by acquiring certain skills.
29-0026: Fighting Stance / Focus on a Single Target
29-0027:
<symbol=case_file_head>Fighting Stance
　　　Knowing when to put up a fighting stance is an essential part of combat.
　　　<color=red>Being in a fighting stance is required to perform certain moves</color> and enables
　　　you to easily strafe around your opponent.
　　　Furthermore, getting into a fighting stance is particularly helpful during
　　　<color=red>one-on-one battles</color>.
　　　<symbol=case_file_lower_than><symbol=button_r1><symbol=case_file_greater_than>

<symbol=case_file_head>Locking onto Enemies
　　　If you enter a fighting stance, you will automatically lock onto the nearest
　　　enemy. When you get too far away from the enemy, or another enemy 
　　　comes between you and the target, you will automatically lock onto a
　　　new target.
　　　<symbol=case_file_lower_than><symbol=button_r1><symbol=case_file_greater_than>
29-0029:
<symbol=case_file_head>How to Quickstep
　　　Although the most basic method of defense is guarding with <symbol=button_l1>, you can
　　　also dodge attacks with a Quickstep.

　　　Not only is it useful against <color=red>attacks that can't be blocked</color>, it also allows you
　　　to circle around to the enemy's blind spot, <color=red>giving you an opening to strike</color>.
　　　
　　　<symbol=case_file_lower_than>Enter a fighting stance with <symbol=button_r1>, use <symbol=button_l_stick> to move in any direction, 
　　　　and press <symbol=button_batsu>.<symbol=case_file_greater_than>
29-0031: Grab Enemies and Weapons to Attack
29-0032:
<symbol=case_file_head>Grabbing Enemies
　　　Grabbing enemies will automatically <color=red>break their guard</color> and temporarily
　　　<color=red>restrict their movement</color>. From there, you can unleash various attacks, 
　　　such as Light/Strong Attacks, throws, and EX Actions.

　　　You can even grab an enemy and basically use them as a meat shield.
　　　Furthermore, you can grab enemies wielding guns or knives to make them
　　　drop those dangerous weapons.
　　　<symbol=case_file_lower_than>Press <symbol=button_maru> when behind an enemy.<symbol=case_file_greater_than>

<symbol=case_file_head>Picking Up Weapons
　　　You can pick up various objects lying around the city and improvise them as
　　　weapons. Not only are weapons useful offensively, they can also 
　　　<color=red>block dangerous attacks that can't be stopped barehandedly</color>.
　　　<symbol=case_file_lower_than>Press <symbol=button_maru> near an object to pick it up and use it as a weapon.<symbol=case_file_greater_than>
29-0033: Grabbing Enemies and Picking Up Weapons
29-0034:
<symbol=case_file_head>Take It to the Extreme
　　　These incredibly powerful techniques are even stronger than the <symbol=button_shikaku> Rush Combo or
　　　the <symbol=button_sankaku> Finishing Blow, and can only be performed by <color=red>consuming the EX Gauge.</color>

　　　<symbol=case_file_lower_than>Press <symbol=button_sankaku> when you see "<symbol=button_sankaku> EX Action" displayed.<symbol=case_file_greater_than>
　　　*See "EX Action" in "Help" for details.
29-0035:
<symbol=case_file_head>EX Gauge
　　　The EX Gauge at the top-left corner gets charged up as Yagami attacks enemies or
　　　taunts them with <symbol=button_l3>.

　　　You can <color=red>prevent EX Actions from activating</color> by holding <symbol=button_l2> if you wish to keep the
　　　EX Gauge charged.
29-0037:
<symbol=case_file_head>Unleash Your Inner Beast
　　　Over the years, Yagami has mastered two distinct combat styles, <color=blue>Crane</color> and
　　　<color=red>Tiger</color>, which he can switch between at any time.
　　　<symbol=case_file_lower_than><symbol=button_down><symbol=case_file_greater_than>

　　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Crane Style
　　　　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow><color=blue>Effective against a group of enemies.</color>
　　　　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow><color=blue>Dishes out quick attacks that cover a wide area.</color>
　　　　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow><color=blue>Possesses an abundance of EX Actions to use against multiple
　　　　　　enemies.</color>

　　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Tiger Style
　　　　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow><color=red>Effective against a single opponent.</color>
　　　　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow><color=red>Delivers powerful attacks against a single enemy that can break
　　　　　　through their guard.</color>
　　　　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow><color=red>Possesses an abundance of EX Actions to use against a single
　　　　　　enemy.</color>
29-0040:
<symbol=case_file_head>Wall Jump
　　　By dashing toward a wall with <symbol=button_batsu>, you can perform a special maneuver that
　　　allows you to <color=red>dodge almost any attack</color>.
　　　<symbol=case_file_lower_than><symbol=button_batsu> Dash toward a wall<symbol=case_file_greater_than>

<symbol=case_file_head>Wall Strike
　　　You can even attack during a Wall Jump. Doing so allows you to <color=red>damage
　　　enemies that are normally invulnerable on the ground</color> as well as perform
　　　certain EX Actions.
　　　<symbol=case_file_lower_than><symbol=button_shikaku>/<symbol=button_sankaku>/<symbol=button_maru> During a Wall Jump<symbol=case_file_greater_than>
　　　*<symbol=button_sankaku>/<symbol=button_maru> Can be learned from the Skills App.
29-0041:
<symbol=case_file_head>Enhance Your Abilities with the Skills App

　　　If you want to make yourself stronger, open up the Pause Menu and
　　　navigate to the Skills App. Note that learning skills requires SP.
　　　*See "Help"<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>"Skills" for details.
29-0043:
<symbol=case_file_head>Mortal Wounds
　　　You may receive a Mortal Wound when hit by bullets or certain enemy attacks
　　　(Deadly Attacks).

　　　While suffering from a Mortal Wound, <color=red>your maximum health is reduced</color> and
　　　cannot be restored by eating or using recovery items.
　　　You can treat Mortal Wounds by visiting a specific doctor somewhere in Kamurocho
　　　or using a <color=green>Medical Kit</color>.
29-0044:
<symbol=case_file_head>Deadly Attacks
　　　Deadly Attacks are <color=red>performed by enemies after their aura flares up intensely.</color> Since
　　　Deadly Attacks inflict Mortal Wounds, do your best to avoid them by Quickstepping
　　　with <symbol=button_r1>+<symbol=button_batsu>, pressing <symbol=button_batsu> to sprint toward a wall and performing a <color=red>Wall Jump</color>,
　　　or pressing <symbol=button_r2> to enter EX Boost. Trying to guard with <symbol=button_l1> will only land you in the
　　　hospital... or worse.
29-0046:
<symbol=case_file_head>Skills for Survival
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Yagami possesses a wide variety of <color=striking>skills and abilities</color> that help him solve his cases.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>There are three types of skills Yagami can learn: <color=striking>Ability, Battle, and Special.</color>

　<symbol=case_file_lower_than>Ability<symbol=case_file_greater_than>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Skills that <color=striking>raise Yagami's base stats</color>, such as Health and Attack.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> There are also skills that further increase Yagami's stats after certain requirements are met.

　<symbol=case_file_lower_than>Battle<symbol=case_file_greater_than>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Consists of a variety of fighting moves, <color=striking>such as EX Actions or alternate variations of finishing moves.</color>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Learn lots of Battle Skills if you want to have an arsenal of flashy and powerful attacks.

　<symbol=case_file_lower_than>Special<symbol=case_file_greater_than>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> A broad category of skills that <color=striking>help you as you explore the city, such as tailing and lockpicking.</color>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> There are many Special Skills that come in handy in unexpected ways, so be sure not to ignore them.
29-0047:
<symbol=case_file_head>It's All in the App
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Use the <color=striking>Skills App</color> located in the Pause Menu to improve Yagami's
　　overall abilities.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Simply open the Skills App and select the skill you want to learn.

　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Note that all skills cost a certain amount of <color=striking>SP</color> to learn.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> There are also a number of skills that remain locked until <color=striking>specific criteria</color>
　　　are met first.
29-0049:
<symbol=case_file_head>How to Acquire SP
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Skill Points, or SP, are necessary in order to learn skills, and can be acquired through the following methods:
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> <color=striking>Clearing missions posted in Case File > Tasks.</color>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> <color=striking>Completing Side Cases.</color>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> <color=striking>Building friendships with the people you meet around town.</color>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> <color=striking>Playing minigames.</color>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> <color=striking>Clearing each type of mission in the KamuroGo App.</color>

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>You may be able to acquire SP in other, unexpected ways as you travel about the city.
29-0050:
<symbol=case_file_head>Unlocking Skills

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>There are some skills that remain locked until certain conditions are met.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>The following can help you on your quest to unlock some of these skills:
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> <color=striking>Acquiring a Skill Book.</color>
　　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Skill Books can be obtained as minigame prizes or as Side Case completion rewards.

　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> <color=striking>Capture a 2D Code.</color>
　　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Use the camera on your phone or drone to take a photo of the 2D Codes found on posters scattered throughout Kamurocho.

　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> <color=striking>Clearing certain events.</color>
　　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Completing Side Cases and improving your relationships with friends.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Meet and interact with as many people as possible and explore Kamurocho to the fullest in order to gain access to all the skills
　　available. Take a step outside and see what the city has to offer.
29-0052:
<symbol=case_file_head>About Tailing

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>When you make some kind of commotion that could attract the target's attention,
　　the <color=striking>Caution Gauge</color> at the top of the screen will fill.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> If the <color=striking>Caution Gauge reaches its limit</color>, then you will fail the mission.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>If you're about to get noticed, take cover behind a building or put more
　　distance between yourself and the target.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> The Caution Gauge will start to go down again once you successfully avoid
　　　detection.
29-0053:
<symbol=case_file_subhead>A countdown timer will display at the top of the screen if you lose sight of
　　your target.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Locate the target before the countdown reaches zero.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead><color=striking>Losing sight of your target will also result in a failure.</color>
29-0055:
<symbol=case_file_head>Beware of Wary Targets

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>As you follow your target, there will be times when they stop and look around.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> If they spot you during this time, their Caution Gauge will fill quickly. Should you
　　　remain in their field of vision by the time it's full, you will fail the mission.
29-0056:
<symbol=case_file_head>Take Care to Take Cover

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>When you see a <color=striking>Cover Spot</color> nearby, press <symbol=button_maru> to go into hiding.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Doing so will keep you out of the target's field of vision and steadily decrease
　　their Caution Gauge.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> However, <color=striking>you won't be able to move while taking cover.</color>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Find the right time to emerge and keep the target in your field of vision so you
　　　don't lose them completely.
29-0058:
<symbol=case_file_head>About Disguises

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>You can mask Yagami's identity with various disguises at certain points in the
　　story.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Simply use the Items App and navigate to the Disguises tab.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>You must have the proper disguise set in your inventory in order to wear
　　　the disguise.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>However, disguises can't be worn all the time.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>They can only be worn when an investigation specifically requires it.
29-0059:
<symbol=case_file_head>Soar Through the Open Skies
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Use the Drone App to operate the drone.
　<symbol=case_file_lower_than>Flight<symbol=case_file_greater_than>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Allows you to fly the drone.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Press <symbol=button_maru> to end your flight.

　<symbol=case_file_lower_than>Customize<symbol=case_file_greater_than>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Allows you to customize your drone and change parts.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow><color=striking>New parts can be developed at the Drone Lab.</color>

　<symbol=case_file_lower_than>Race Record<symbol=case_file_greater_than>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Allows you to check the results of all the Drone Leagues you've competed
　　　in until now.

　<symbol=case_file_lower_than>Operation<symbol=case_file_greater_than>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Allows you to change the controls when operating your drone.
29-0060:
<symbol=case_file_head>Chasing Targets

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>There are times when Yagami must chase a target down in order to complete
　　an investigation.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>During a chase sequence, Yagami will run forward automatically.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead><color=striking>The only condition for failing is if the target gets too far away from you.</color>
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Close the distance between your target and evade obstacles by using <symbol=button_l_stick> to
　　move sideways as well as pressing the correct buttons at the right time.
29-0061:
<symbol=case_file_head>Capturing Targets

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>During chase sequences where you need to capture the target, press the displayed
　　button as soon as you get close to apprehend them.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead><color=striking>This will satisfy your objective.</color>
29-0062: Restaurants: The Importance of Regular Meals
29-0063:
<symbol=case_file_head>Eat to Recover Your Health

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Chow down at one of the many restaurants in Kamurocho to recover your health.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> The amount of health recovered depends on what you order.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>If your health is already full, you won't be able to eat.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Also, try getting to know the staff at each of the restaurants you visit; they may end up giving you access to their secret menu.
29-0064: Restaurants: Pros and Cons of Getting Drunk
29-0065:
<symbol=case_file_head>To Drink, or Not to Drink

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Kamurocho's many bars and dining establishments offer a wide selection of alcohol to choose from.


　<symbol=case_file_subhead>When Yagami decides to drink, his intoxication level will rise.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> <color=striking>The EX Gauge charges up faster when Yagami is drunk.</color>

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Yagami will go through several stages of intoxication depending on how much alcohol he consumes.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Once Yagami consumes a certain amount of alcohol, <color=striking>he won't be able to drink anymore until you give him time to sober up</color>.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> However, he can acquire several skills that raise his alcohol tolerance and make him more functional at the bar.
29-0066:
<symbol=case_file_head>Shop till You Drop

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Shops like Don Quijote and Poppo offer a wide variety of items at affordable prices.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>At Le Marche, you can find expensive brand-name goods that would make the perfect gift for that special lady in your life.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>At Ebisu Pawn Shop, you can purchase various knickknacks for Yagami's office and materials. You can also sell items here
　　to earn some extra cash.
29-0067:
<symbol=case_file_head>Use Taxis to Cut Down Travel Time

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>All you need is 410 yen and a clean-cut, professional-looking taxi driver will take you to your destination of choice.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>At certain points in the story, there will be times where you need to take a taxi to reach destinations outside Kamurocho.
29-0069:
<symbol=case_file_head>Get to Know Your Stomping Grounds

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>There are numerous venues in town called Hangout Spots which act as Yagami's primary sources of information.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>By frequenting Hangout Spots, you can <color=striking>gather new information on investigations</color> or simply have a chat with some interesting
　　people.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Some of these people may end up becoming <color=striking>powerful allies</color> on your quest to bring justice to the streets, provided you spend
　　enough time with them.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead><color=striking>Check the <symbol=map_icon_park> icon at the top of the map to locate all the Hangout Spots.
29-0070:
<symbol=case_file_head>When Kamuro Goes with You

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>KamuroGo is a smartphone application developed by the Kamurocho Chamber of Commerce.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>This app was developed to foster local participation in municipal activities and distribute SP to active members of the community.

　<symbol=case_file_lower_than>Profile<symbol=case_file_greater_than>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Displays a record of your activities around town and how many missions you've cleared.

　<symbol=case_file_lower_than>Shop Missions<symbol=case_file_greater_than>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Lists all the shops and restaurants and how many times you've used their services.
　　　Each venue has missions you can clear in order to gain SP. 
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>If you use a certain amount of money at some stores, you will be awarded a "KamuroGo Coupon."
　　　You can check the requirements in the store screen.

　<symbol=case_file_lower_than>City Missions<symbol=case_file_greater_than>　　
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Summarizes your activities in Kamurocho.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>You'll gain SP with each mission completed.
29-0071:
<symbol=case_file_head>Helping You Find Your Way

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>The Map App has the following handy features:

　<symbol=case_file_lower_than>Search<symbol=case_file_greater_than>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Open the map and press <symbol=button_sankaku> to bring up the search window.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>You can find more details about a particular venue by looking it up in the search results.

　<symbol=case_file_lower_than>Location Info<symbol=case_file_greater_than>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Placing your cursor over a Map Icon and pressing <symbol=button_shikaku> will also give you details about that location.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Pressing <symbol=button_decide> while having that information displayed will allow you set that location as a waypoint.

　<symbol=case_file_lower_than>Setting a Waypoint<symbol=case_file_greater_than>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>While looking at the map, press <symbol=button_decide> to set a waypoint at wherever your cursor is.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>After a waypoint is set, the map will provide directions on the fastest way to get there.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>You can remove the waypoint by placing the cursor anywhere on the map and pressing <symbol=button_decide>.
29-0072:
<symbol=case_file_head>Quickstart the Next Big Thing

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Quickstarter is the latest crowdfunding app that puts the power of investing in the palm of your hand.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>By helping each project reach their goals, you can witness the development of various new items and facilities firsthand.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>As such, using Quickstarter will give you special access to items and facilities that would otherwise not exist.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>So it may be beneficial to support your favorite projects with a healthy influx of cash whenever you can afford it.
29-0073:
<symbol=case_file_head>Review the Facts

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Case File is an app installed on Yagami's phone that automatically sorts and organizes information.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Check this app whenever you're not sure what to do next.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Case File is particularly handy when you want to progress the story.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>You can also check what you need to do for Side Cases as well.

　<symbol=case_file_lower_than>Main Case<symbol=case_file_greater_than>
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>You can check the People, Evidence, and Details concerning the main story. 
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Whenever a Main Case category is updated, "!" will be displayed next to it.

　<symbol=case_file_lower_than>Side Case<symbol=case_file_greater_than>
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>You can check the Personnel, Evidence, and Details concerning your various Side Cases.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Whenever a Side Case category is updated, "!" will be displayed next to it.
29-0074:
<symbol=case_file_head>About Saving

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>You can save investigation records with the Save App. Wow!

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Simply open the Save app and choose a slot where you'd like to save your data.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> If you have Autosave turned on, your progress will be automatically saved as you play through the game.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> You can still save manually through the Save App even with Autosave turned on.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow><color=striking> Be mindful that if you have Autosave turned off, your progress will not be saved unless you use the Save App.</color>
29-0075:
<symbol=case_file_head>Blackjack

　<symbol=case_file_lower_than>Basic Rules<symbol=case_file_greater_than>

　　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Blackjack is a game where you get the numbers of your cards as close as you can to 21.
　　<symbol=case_file_subhead>You win if the total of your hand is closer to 21 than that of the dealer.
　　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> A two-card hand consisting of an Ace and either a King, Queen, Jack, or 10 is called a Blackjack.
　　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> This is the best possible hand in the game, and will return 2.5 times your original bet (unless the dealer also has Blackjack).

　　<symbol=case_file_subhead>If you go over 21, you bust, meaning you lose.


　<symbol=case_file_lower_than>Counting Card Values<symbol=case_file_greater_than>

　　<symbol=case_file_subhead>An Ace can be valued either at 1 or 11, depending on which is more convenient for your hand.
　　<symbol=case_file_subhead>10, J, Q, and K are all valued at 10.
29-0076:
<symbol=case_file_head>Blackjack Terminology

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Hit
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Draw a card and add it to your hand.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Stand
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Stay with your current hand.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Split
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>If you are dealt two of the same cards, you can choose to split them into two separate hands.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>You will then play both hands at the same time.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Double Down
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>This option allows you to double your bet after seeing the hand dealt to you.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>You must draw an additional card if you choose to do so. This is most commonly used when your hand value totals 11.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Surrender
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Select this option to forfeit your current hand.

Omaha Hold'em is a poker game in which you build five-card hands
from nine cards (two out of four hole cards, plus three out of five
community cards).

<color=mg_relu_topic>How to Win</color>
•Have the strongest hand at the showdown.

29-0082:
In the first round, each player is dealt two hole cards. Three
community cards are dealt in the second round. The fourth and fifth
community cards are dealt in the third and fourth rounds, respectively.

<color=mg_relu_topic>Advancing to the Next Round</color>
•All players have placed bets of the same amount.
•The turn has been checked around.

At the end of the fourth round, all players reveal their hands in a
showdown. The player with the strongest hand wins.
29-0084:
<color=mg_relu_topic>Possible Actions in Each Round</color>
　•Bet: Bet a fixed amount of chips.
　•Call: Bet the same amount of chips as the previous player.
•Raise: Bet more chips than the previous player.
　•Check: Don't bet, in which case the next player goes.
　•Fold: Stop betting and retire from the current hand.

*You may place a bet if none of the other players have bet yet.
*You can check if none of the other players have bet yet, or if all
the other players call the big blind.
29-0085:
A big blind and little blind are forced bets at the beginning of a
hand that must be made by the first and second players that get the
dealer button after the current dealer. (The dealer button rotates
clockwise after each hand.)

<color=mg_relu_topic>Bet Amounts Each Round</color>
•Big Blind: Minimum bet
•Little Blind: Half the minimum bet

29-0105:

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>You will not be able to shoot while you're reloading or if the crosshairs aren't
　　displayed.

<symbol=case_file_lower_than>Grenades<symbol=case_file_greater_than>

　　stage.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Shooting a metal drum while at maximum grenade capacity will increase your

　　aren't displayed.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>With <color=striking>Online Ranking</color>, you can <color=striking>view the best finish times of racers across the world.</color>


<symbol=case_file_lower_than>Register Finish Time<symbol=case_file_greater_than>
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>If you would like to register your own finish time, select Test Flight and choose Online Ranking.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Once finished, you will be asked if you want to register your finish time, to which you can choose "Yes."

　<color=striking>* Registering finish time requires an internet connection.</color>
29-0140: Challenge racers from across the world with Online Ranking
29-0141:
<symbol=case_file_head>Get Ready to Roll the Dice in Virtual Reality

　<symbol=case_file_subhead><color=striking>Paradise</color> is a cutting-edge entertainment center where you can play
　　<color=striking>Dice & Cube</color>, a virtual reality game based on sugoroku.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Talk to the receptionist and <color=striking>use Play Passes</color> whenever you want to play.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>More courses and rulesets are unlocked as you clear each course, leaving you
　　with six courses in total.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>You can only get a reward the first time you clear a course.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Lucky players may even come across extra hard-to-find drone parts!
29-0142:
<symbol=case_file_head>Acquire a Play Pass

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>You will need a special voucher called a <color=striking>Play Pass</color> in order to play Dice & Cube.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> <color=striking>Each course requires a certain number of Play Passes.</color>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> This number differs depending on the course you choose.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Play Passes can be acquired in various ways, such as getting good scores in minigames.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> There's also a rumor circulating about a <color=striking>Free Pass</color> which allows you play an unlimited number of games...
　　　It might be found where you least expect it, so be sure check every nook and cranny of the city.
29-0145:
<symbol=case_file_head>Master the Keys to Unlocking

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Simply using the correct key is one method of opening a locked door.
　
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Out of all the keys you own, <color=striking>choose the one that fits the keyhole and press
　　the corresponding button.</color>

　　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> If you choose the correct key, the door will open.
　　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> If you choose the wrong key, the door stays closed and you will have to
　　　　choose a key again.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>You'll acquire more keys as you progress through the story.
29-0147:
<symbol=case_file_head>On the Unscrupulous Picking of Locks

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Lock picking is a questionable yet sometimes necessary measure for opening
　　locked doors.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Use a pick to adjust the notch of the pins so that they line up with the
　　shear line (colored red).</color>
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Each pin has a set position of the shear line.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead><color=striking>You can open the lock by aligning all the shear lines.</color>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> If you hold the pin too high, <color=striking>all the pins will reset back to their
　　　original position</color>, including the ones you've already adjusted.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Different door locks have a different number of pins.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Some locks have to be picked within a given time limit, or else it's game over.
29-0149:
<symbol=case_file_head>Work Those Thumbs

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Using the thumb turn bypass is yet another way to open a locked door.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Slip a <color=striking>Thin Wire</color> through the door's gap and turn the knob on the other side of
　　the door to unlock it.
　　*<color=striking>If you don't have a thin wire, you won't be able to do a thumb turn bypass.</color>

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Use <input_device=KEYBOARD_AND_MOUSE><symbol=mouse_moveint></input_device><input_device_not=KEYBOARD_AND_MOUSE><symbol=button_l_stick> and <symbol=button_r_stick></input_device_not> to follow the icon within the red frame as shown in the left
　　figure.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> When you match <input_device=KEYBOARD_AND_MOUSE><symbol=mouse_moveint></input_device><input_device_not=KEYBOARD_AND_MOUSE><symbol=button_l_stick> and <symbol=button_r_stick></input_device_not> to the icon, <color=striking>the icon will automatically start
　　　moving.</color>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> <color=striking>Match <input_device=KEYBOARD_AND_MOUSE><symbol=mouse_moveint></input_device><input_device_not=KEYBOARD_AND_MOUSE><symbol=button_l_stick> and <symbol=button_r_stick></input_device_not> to the movement of the icon.</color>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> If you don't match the icon's movement, you'll have to start from the
　　　beginning.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>The number of inputs as well as their specific combinations will vary with
　　each door.
29-0150:
<symbol=case_file_head>Accepting Side Cases

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Yagami can take on various job requests known as Side Cases at the Yagami
　　Detective Agency.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> <color=striking>Check the office bulletin board</color> to see your currently available Side Cases.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> In order to make more Side Cases available, <color=striking>build rapport with the locals
　　and improve your reputation</color>.
29-0152:
<symbol=case_file_head>Music That Soothes the Soul

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Every good detective has a vintage record player in the office, so put a record
　　on and jam out to your favorite tunes.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> The music will keep playing as long as you stay inside the office.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> You can find new records all throughout Kamurocho.
29-0153:
<symbol=case_file_head>A Blast from the Past

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Whether you consider it a good bargain or a weak moment of impulse buying,
　　the fact remains that Yagami possesses a fully functional,
　　state-of-the-art Out Run machine.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Fun fact: This very Out Run machine was almost taken by his landlord because
　　he couldn't pay his rent... on multiple occasions.

　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Know what else is cool? You can play Out Run for free!
29-0155:
<symbol=case_file_head>Just Like Mom Used to Make

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Tomioka-san will occasionally make you food and leave it in your refrigerator.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>When you eat one of Tomioka-san's dishes, you'll recover some of your health.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>So make sure to pop open that fridge whenever you stop by the office.

　<symbol=case_file_lower_than>Rie Tomioka<symbol=case_file_greater_than>
　　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Owner of Building One, where the Yagami Detective Agency is located.
29-0157:
<symbol=case_file_head>You've Got A Lot of Mail!

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Some fun items have been sent to Yagami's office to enhance the Judgment experience.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>These can be claimed from the dropbox just outside Yagami's office. Have fun!
29-0159:
<symbol=case_file_head>Topic Talks

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>As you enjoy your time together, you may enter a <color=striking>Topic Talk</color> while having
　　a conversation. Select the choices you think will make your girlfriend
　　happy to fill your Intimacy Gauge.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Occasionally, one of the choices during a Topic Talk will be <color=striking>locked</color>.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Locked choices are only available once you reach a certain level of trust.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>However, once you unlock these topics, you'll be able to listen to her secrets,
　　concerns, and perhaps a few <color=striking>intimate details</color>?
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Aim to impress her with your sharp wit and vast knowledge, and show her the
　　kind of gentleman (or bad boy) you really are!
29-0160:
<symbol=case_file_head>Get the Full Scoop

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>In Photo Missions, your goal is to investigate certain incidents and capture the
　　decisive moment on camera.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Take a picture that <color=striking>ticks off all the checkboxes</color> on the right side of the screen.

　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> <color=striking>Be careful: if you take a picture without satisfying all the conditions, it will
　　　result in a game over.</color>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Therefore, check your surroundings and look for the best possible camera
　　　angle that allows you to take a picture that satisfies all the criteria.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> <color=striking>Note that you won't be able to take a picture until you fulfill at least one
　　　condition.</color>


<symbol=case_file_head>Get the Best Shot to Gain a Bonus

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>On top of ticking off all the checkboxes, if you capture a photo that <color=striking>perfectly
　　meets the client's demands</color>, you'll gain some SP as a bonus.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Consider the contents carefully and capture that perfect picture.
29-0161:
<symbol=case_file_head>About Active Search Mode

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Active Search Mode is used when investigating crime scenes, checking facts, and
　　scouring for evidence.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>You'll operate in first-person view during this mode. Use the objectives displayed on
　　the right of the screen to help you figure out what you need to investigate.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> There are times when you must stand in place and observe the area without
　　　moving around.
29-0162:
<symbol=case_file_subhead>Move the crosshairs over to suspicious areas and hold <symbol=button_r2> to hone in on them.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> <color=striking>An "Examine" icon will appear if there's something for you to check out.</color>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Press <symbol=button_decide> to examine that spot.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Examine various pieces of evidence and satisfy all the objectives to complete your
　　investigation.
29-0163:
<symbol=case_file_head>Get Your Hands on the Latest Drone Parts

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>The Drone Lab is a facility where you can develop new parts for your drone.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Each part requires a certain amount of <color=striking>materials and money</color> in order to
　　be developed.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> The materials and amount of money required differ from part to part.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Gather materials by purchasing them in shops, solving Side Cases,
　　　interacting with friends, or getting good scores on minigames.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>The following types of parts can be developed:
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> <color=striking>Frame</color>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> <color=striking>Motor</color>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> <color=striking>Propeller</color>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> <color=striking>Turbo
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> <color=striking>ESC</color> (Electronic Speed Control)
29-0164: Selfie: How to Change Your Expression
29-0165:
<symbol=case_file_head>How to Take a Selfie

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Open up the Camera App and press <symbol=button_l3> to switch to the front camera.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Pressing <symbol=button_l3> again will take you back to the rear camera.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>By using the front camera, you can take a selfie.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>You can change Yagami's expressions as follows:
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> <symbol=button_left>  Troubled Yagami
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> <symbol=button_right>  Angry Yagami
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> <symbol=button_up>  Pleasant Yagami
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> <symbol=button_down>  Classic Yagami

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Find the right location and lose yourself in the moment to really nail that selfie.
29-0167:
<symbol=case_file_head>Be Intense

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>During Selfie Mode, you can make even more intense expressions.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>While taking pictures with the front camera, press the directional buttons to change Yagami's facial expression. If you press
　　the same directional button again, his expression will grow even more intense.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Press <symbol=button_left> twice <symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Bamboozled Yagami
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Press <symbol=button_right> twice <symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Furious Yagami
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Press <symbol=button_up> twice <symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Exuberant Yagami

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>So if your picture needs that little extra something, try making an extra-intense expression.
29-0169:
<symbol=case_file_head>When Board Games Get Real

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Dice & Cube is a fusion of sugoroku and VR technology that drops you into a futuristic version of Kamurocho where the roll of the
　　dice determines your reality.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Items acquired during gameplay can be converted into real money after the game is finished.
29-0171:
<symbol=case_file_head>Choose From Two Different Rulesets

　<symbol=case_file_lower_than><color=striking>Standard</color><symbol=case_file_greater_than>

　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Enjoy a more <color=striking>casual</color> play style compared to the Challenge ruleset.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Every space on the board activates a mission, such as battle or lockpicking.


　<symbol=case_file_lower_than><color=striking>Challenge</color><symbol=case_file_greater_than>

　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> A ruleset with <color=striking>higher difficulty, but better rewards</color>.


　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Regardless of which ruleset you choose, reaching the end with a higher number of dice will net you a nice bonus.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>However, if you run out of dice before reaching the end, <color=striking>the game will be over</color>.
29-0173:
<symbol=case_file_head>Roll the Dice

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Figure A on the left represents the dice.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Press <symbol=button_decide> to roll the dice.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Press <symbol=button_decide> again to stop it.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>The number of pips that appear (1 through 6) represents the number of spaces you
　　can move.
29-0174:
<symbol=case_file_head>Mind the Dice

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Whenever you roll the dice, the number on the left (Figure B) will decrease.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> This number represents how many times you can roll the dice for the remainder
　　　of the game.
29-0176:
<symbol=case_file_head>Bow Down to the King of Koro-nyans!


　<symbol=case_file_subhead><color=striking>King Koro-nyan</color> is the leader of the Koro-nyan tribe, and governs them from his
　　　virtual cat-stle.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> King Koro-nyan appears in both the Middle and Long courses.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>If you come in contact with King Koro-nyan, a bonus event called <color=striking>Koro-nyan
　　Mode</color> will be triggered (see page 6 for details).

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Furthermore, King Koro-nyan will restore all your HP and even heal Mortal
　　Wounds that you've received in battle.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>On rare occasions, golden enemies will appear during battle. Defeat them to
　　cause King Koro-nyan to spawn somewhere on the board.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>If you manage to spot King Koro-nyan, make sure to chase him down!
29-0178:
<symbol=case_file_head>The Lone Wanderer of Virtual Kamurocho

　<symbol=case_file_subhead><color=striking>Kuro-nyan</color> is a mischievous digital thief that preys on delicious
　　player data.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Kuro-nyan appears in both the Middle and Long courses.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>If you come in contact with Kuro-nyan, <color=striking>all your items will be taken away</color>.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>After stealing your items, Kuro-nyan will flee to another space on
　　　the board.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Encountering Kuro-nyan after chasing him down will trigger a battle sequence.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>If you win, you will reclaim your stolen items.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Moreover, you may even gain a bonus along with your victory.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>On rare occasions, purple enemies will appear during battle. If you fail to
　　defeat them, a new Kuro-nyan will spawn somewhere on the board.
29-0179:
<symbol=case_file_head>Get Ready for a Big Payout!

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>If you manage to come in contact with King Koro-nyan, <color=striking>Koro-nyan Mode</color> will
　　activate.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>During Koro-nyan Mode, every space will automatically turn into Koro-nyan
　　Spaces.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Each Koro-nyan Space triggers a bonus challenge that deals out huge rewards
　　upon completion.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Koro-nyan Mode <color=striking>ends after three turns</color>.
30-0001:
<symbol=case_file_head>Losing Battles Gets You Booted Back to the Start

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Many spaces in Dice & Cube will trigger a battle once you step on them.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>If you get defeated during battle or fail to win within the time limit, <color=striking>you will be penalized by getting sent back to the
　　starting point</color>.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>However, your health will be fully replenished.
　　　 *On the other hand, Mortal Wounds will not be healed.

<symbol=case_file_head>Keep the Dice Rolling

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>If you run out of dice rolls, <color=striking>the game will end</color>.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>When the number of dice reaches 0, the following penalties will be applied:
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow><color=striking>Standard Course</color>: You must <color=striking>cash in</color> all your items.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow><color=striking>Challenge Course</color>: You will <color=striking>lose</color> all your items.
30-0003:
<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>Dice Plus Space</color>　

<symbol=case_file_subhead>Stepping on these will increase your amount of dice.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>The amount increased varies with the space.
30-0004:
<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>Dice Minus Space</color>　

<symbol=case_file_subhead>Stepping on these will decrease your amount of dice.
　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>The amount decreased varies with the space.
30-0006:
<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>Gift Space</color>

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Stepping on these allows you to receive items.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>The items you received will be cashed in once you finish the game.
30-0007:
<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>Battle Space</color>

<symbol=case_file_subhead>Stepping on these will trigger a battle.
　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>The battle rules vary with each space.
　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>More stars means greater difficulty.
　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>If you win the battle, the number of stars on the space will be added to your total
　　amount of dice.
　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>However, if you are defeated or can't win within the time limit, you will be
　　returned to the starting point.
30-0008:
<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>Safe Space</color>

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Stepping on these will present you with a locked safe.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>You must then use your lock picking skills to open the safe within the given
　　time limit.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>If you succeed within the time limit, you will receive a valuable item.
30-0009:
<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>Warp Space</color>

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Stepping on these will warp you to a different space on the board.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Landing on the space you warped to again will take you back to the space you
　　came from.
30-0010:
<symbol=case_file_head>During your VR adventure, you will engage in a variety of Battle Missions, each with their own unique set of rules.
　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Every Battle Mission has a <color=striking>time limit.</color>
　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> If you don't meet the conditions within the given time limit, you will fail the mission regardless of your remaining health.


<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>Types of Battle Missions</color>

　<symbol=case_file_subhead><color=striking>Locked Style Battle</color>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> A battle that restricts you to only one combat style.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> You will not be able to switch styles at any time during this battle.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead><color=striking>Dire Battle</color>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> A battle where every enemy attack inflicts a Mortal Wound.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Mortal Wounds can be healed if you encounter King Koro-nyan.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead><color=striking>Drone Battle</color>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> A battle that pits your drone against an enemy's to try and shoot them down.
30-0012:
<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>More Types of Battle Missions</color>

　<symbol=case_file_subhead><color=striking>Railgun Battle</color>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> A battle where you fight solely with a railgun.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> You cannot remove this weapon for the duration of the fight. 
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> You cannot change combat styles or enter EX Boost either.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead><color=striking>Double Stick Battle</color>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> A battle where you fight solely with a double stick.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> You cannot remove this weapon for the duration of the fight. 
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> You cannot change combat styles or enter EX Boost either.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead><color=striking>Sword Battle</color>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> A battle where you fight solely with a sword.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> You cannot remove this weapon for the duration of the fight.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> You cannot change combat styles or enter EX Boost either.
30-0013:
<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>Battles During Koro-nyan Mode</color>

　<symbol=case_file_subhead><color=striking>Destruction Battle</color>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> A battle exclusive to Koro-nyan Mode.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> This mission challenges you to destroy as many objects as possible within the time limit.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> The more objects you wreck, the more prizes you get.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead><color=striking>Knockout Battle</color>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> A battle exclusive to Koro-nyan mode.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> This mission challenges you to hit as many enemies as possible within the time limit.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> The more attacks you land, the more prizes you get.
30-0014:
<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>Special Enemies</color>

　<symbol=case_file_subhead><color=striking>Golden Enemies</color>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> In rare cases, a <color=striking>golden enemy</color> may appear. Defeating them causes King Koro-nyan to spawn!
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> If you run into King Koro-nyan, you will activate<color=striking> Koro-nyan Mode</color>.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> So if you ever come across a golden enemy during battle, kick his butt!

　<symbol=case_file_subhead><color=striking>Purple Enemies</color>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> In rare cases, a <color=striking>purple enemy</color> may appear.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> If you end the battle without defeating them, Kuro-nyan will spawn. (He's the bad kitty.)
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> If you encounter Kuro-nyan, <color=striking>all your items will be stolen from you.</color>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> So if you see a purple enemy, kick his butt too!
30-0015:
<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>Kamurocho's Newest Attraction</color>

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>The Drone League is a contest that pits you against some of the most
　　competitive drone racers in the country.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Each race has 10 participants.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Customize, control, and compete with your favorite drone in hopes of
　　winning it all.
30-0017:
<symbol=case_file_head>A. <color=striking>Time Limit</color>
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>The timer will begin counting as soon as the race starts. If it reaches 0 before
　　you clear the course, you'll be disqualified.
　　*More time will be added with every lap around the course.
<symbol=case_file_head> B. <color=striking>Current Rank</color>
<symbol=case_file_head> C. <color=striking>Course Minimap</color>
<symbol=case_file_head> D. <color=striking>Durability</color>
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Decreases as you run into obstacles. Once it reaches 0, your drone will break
　　and you will be disqualified from the race.
<symbol=case_file_head> E. <color=striking>Turbo Gauge</color>
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Gradually accumulates over time. Once it reaches full, you can press <symbol=button_r1> to
　　gain a temporary boost of speed.

30-0019:
<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>Boost Points</color>

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>By passing through Boost Points (blue rings), your drone will gain a temporary speed
　　boost.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Passing through a Boost Point while using Turbo will trigger a <color=striking>Barrel Roll</color>, which
　　grants your drone an even greater level of acceleration accompanied by a
　　stylish spin.
30-0020:
<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>Repair Points</color>

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Passing through Repair Points (green rings), will replenish your drone's Durability.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Your drone won't be able to fly if your Durability runs out, which means you'll be
　　disqualified from the race.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Thus, it is important to pass through Repair Points whenever your drone is
　　severely damaged.
30-0021: Drone Race <symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Boost Points and Repair Points
30-0022:
<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>Exciting League System</color>

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>The Drone League is made up of the five leagues displayed to the left.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Each league consists of five to ten courses, and whoever has the most total
　　points after completing all courses wins that league.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>The winner then advances to a higher league.
　　*There are no demotions in league competitions.
30-0024:
<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>Costs and Limits</color>
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>All drone parts except for frames have an equipment cost.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Frames, on the other hand, have a Cost Limit, which determines the parts you
　　can equip. Naturally, better frames have a higher Cost Limit that allow for
　　the installation of higher-grade parts.

<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>Durability</color>
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Once your drone's Durability runs out, it breaks. So this stat is very important.

<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>Speed</color>
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Determines the maximum speed of your drone.

<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>Handling</color>
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Affects your drone's overall maneuverability (i.e. how well it can turn) as well
　　as its rate of acceleration.

<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>Turbo</color>
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Affects how quickly your drone's Turbo fills up.
30-0026:
<symbol=case_file_head>If you find yourself having difficulty winning a race, try <color=striking>customizing your drone</color>.

<symbol=case_file_head>By handing over materials and paying money at Drone Lab, you'll be able to
　create new parts.

<symbol=case_file_head>Customize your drone to suit the course you're racing on; for example, focus on
　Speed for long, straight courses, or prioritize Handling on courses with
　lots of curves.

<symbol=case_file_head>After you finish customizing, try out how your drone feels in a Test Flight or
　a Single Race before going all-in on a league competition.

　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> As rewards from Side Cases/Friend Events
　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Purchasing them from Ebisu Pawn
　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> As rewards from minigames
　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Finding them around the city
30-0028:
<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>Play Against Unforeseen Rivals</color>

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>By choosing Online Ranking at the front desk, you'll be able to view the
　　finish times uploaded by racers all over the world.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>You can also upload your own data from Test Flights or Single Races.
　　<color=striking>* Internet connection is required for Online Ranking.</color>
30-0031:
<symbol=case_file_head>About Tailing

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>When you make some kind of commotion that could attract the target's attention,
　　the <color=striking>Caution Gauge</color> displayed at the top of the screen will fill.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> If the <color=striking>Caution Gauge fills completely</color>, you will fail the mission.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>If you're about to get noticed, take cover behind a building or object or put more
　　distance between yourself and the target.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> The Caution Gauge will start to go down if you successfully avoid 
　　　detection.
30-0032:
<symbol=case_file_subhead>A countdown timer will display at the top of the screen if you lose sight of
　　your target.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Get the target in your sights before the countdown reaches zero.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead><color=striking>Losing sight of your target will also result in a failure.</color>
30-0033:
<symbol=case_file_head>Take Care to Take Cover

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>When you see a <color=striking>Cover Spot</color> nearby, press <symbol=button_maru> to go into hiding.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Doing so will keep you out of the target's field of vision and steadily decrease their
　　Caution Gauge.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> However, <color=striking>you won't be able to move while taking cover.</color>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Find the right time to emerge and keep the target in your field of vision so you
　　　 don't lose them completely.
30-0035:
<symbol=case_file_head>Pilot the Yagami Detective Agency's Latest Piece of Tech

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>A drone is a miniature unmanned reconnaisance aircraft that comes equipped with a camera.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Yagami and Kaito apparently refer to it as "the pigeon."
　　　 If you look closely, there's even a pigeon doodle drawn on the done by Kaito...

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Anyway, the drone can be controlled through the Drone app on Yagami's smartphone.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Open the Drone app on the smartphone menu and select Flight to start piloting the drone.

30-0151:
<symbol=case_file_head>EX Boost
　　　By activating EX Boost, Yagami will enter a special state in which his overall
　　　abilities are enhanced and he can perform special EX Actions.

　　　During EX Boost, <color=red>your attack speed is increased</color> and <color=red>you are less likely to
　　　recoil from attacks</color> since <color=red>the EX Gauge absorbs your damage (Even Deadly
　　　Attacks.)</color>. Be sure to use EX Actions and EX Boost accordingly to
　　　suit your needs in a fight.
　　　<symbol=case_file_lower_than>Press <symbol=button_r2> once the EX Gauge is charged up to activate EX Boost.<symbol=case_file_greater_than>

　　　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Changing Styles during EX Boost will allow you to cancel out of

30-0152:
<symbol=case_file_head>Gangsters Don't Ask Questions
　　On the rough and grimy streets of Kamurocho, people might pick a fight with
　　you for no reason at all. Although you can probably just ignore most of these
　　punks, defeating them will get you items as well as valuable SP.

<symbol=case_file_head>About the Keihin Gang
　　The Keihin Gang is a group of reckless thugs that recently made their mark
　　on Kamurocho. Not even the yakuza can handle the chaos they leave in their
　　wake, so residents have been forced to bow their heads and accept it.

　　You will occasionally run into Keihin Gang leaders, who are several cuts
　　above the rest of their lackluster crew, so be sure to use the Skills App
　　to prepare yourself for battle.
30-0154:
<symbol=case_file_head>Watch Your Back
　　Depending on where you are in the story and how much time has passed, there
　　may be more Keihin Gang members swarming the streets than usual. When the
　　Threat Level is present, your chance of encountering Keihin Gang members
　　is higher.

　　Whenever the Threat Level is onscreen, expect a lot of trouble as you walk
　　around town. In order to lower the Threat Level, either defeat a Keihin Gang
　　leader or allow some time to pass.
30-0155:
<symbol=case_file_head>How to Make Keihin Gang Leaders Appear
　　When the Threat Level is onscreen, up to four leaders from the Keihin Gang
　　will appear somewhere in the city.

　　In order to reduce the number of gangsters prowling around town, you must
　　either defeat those leaders or wait for some time to pass. However, if you do
　　defeat the leaders, you'll receive a reward from the locals.
30-0156:
<symbol=case_file_head>Call In the Squad
　　If you build your relationships with the locals and end up becoming friends,
　　you'll sometimes learn a Cooperative EX Action with them.

　　Cooperative EX Actions are like regular EX Actions, but they have to be pulled
　　off with the help of a local ally. Each of these powerful moves will help turn
　　the tides of battle in your favor. So if you find someone in town that you
　　think would make a good ally, definitely get them on your side.
30-0158:
<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>Understanding the Wareme Ruleset</color>

<symbol=case_file_subhead><color=striking>This is a quarter-length game that utilizes wareme and negative points. Just so you know, this is pretty high-level mahjong.</color>

　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Quarter game: Each player will only be the dealer once (instead of twice), assuming the dealer doesn't win.

<symbol=case_file_subhead><color=striking>Wareme</color>

<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>The player whose wall was broken (it's random) at the beginning of a hand becomes the wareme for that hand.
<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>The wareme always pays or receives double the amount of points.
 For example, if you are a dealer and your hand would be worth 4,000 points, if you are the wareme, it is worth 8,000 points.

<symbol=case_file_subhead><color=striking>Going negative is a 10,000 point penalty. (Harsh.)</color>

<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>If your score becomes negative, you must pay 10,000 points to the person who went out.
  *If you get exactly 0 points, no penalty incurs.
30-0160:
<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>The starting score is 25,000 points, with a point baseline of 30,000 points. (If there is no winner, it becomes a draw.)</color>   
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Players will start out with 25,000 points. When the game ends, the total score will be calculated using 30,000 points as
　　the baseline.

<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>Oka gets the jackpot, whereas Uma is not considered.</color>
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>The starting score is 25,000 points per player for a total of 100,000 points. The point baseline is 30,000 points per player for
　　a total of 120,000 points. The 20,000 point difference is awarded as a jackpot to the player who places first.

<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>Ari-ari Ruleset</color>
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Both Kuitan (allowing All Simples with discards) and Atozuke (being allowed to go out as long as you will have a yaku
　　afterwards) take effect in this ruleset.

<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>2 doras and uradora are available (both use the succeeding tiles of indicators).</color>
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Usually, only 1 dora is visible. But in this mode, two dora are visible from the start of the game, and there are 2 ura-doras as well.

<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>Kandora Takes Immediate Effect</color>
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>The dora flipped when kan is called becomes effective immediately.

<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>Allows for sacred discards</color>
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Even if your winning tile is in your discard pile, you can call riichi (or open riichi) and go out with a tsumo. (No rons.)
　　Payment for open riichi is considered a yakuman.
30-0161:
<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>Allow tiles to be passed after a riichi is called.</color>
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Players can pass over a winning discard tile and still win, but only with a tsumo.

<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>Ron will follow turn order. (Triple ron is invalid.)</color>
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>If two players call for a ron, the priority is given to the person starting counterclockwise from the player who discarded
　　the ron tile.
　　For example:
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Calling ron on a discard by East (Dealer): In order of South, West, North
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Calling ron on a discard by South: In order of West, North, East
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Calling ron on a discard by West: In order of North, East, South
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>Calling ron on a discard by North: In order of East, South, West

<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>After four draw results, a dealer can end the game.</color>
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>If all players do not succeed, dealership does not change.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>If the dealer does not succeed, the round is invalid.
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Additionally, if the last dealer has gone out, they can decide whether or not to add bonuses.
30-0162:
<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>Four player riichi is nullified</color>
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>If all four players declare a riichi, that round becomes invalid.

<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>Nine Tiles, Nine Types & Quadruple Wind Discard are also nullified</color>
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Nine Tiles, Nine Types
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>The rule that would allow players to invalidate the round based on an unfavorable hand is not in play. 

　<symbol=case_file_subhead><color=striking>Quadruple Wind Discard</color>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>If during the first go-around without a chi, pon or kan, all players discard the same wind tile, the round becomes invalid.

<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>Empty Tenpai is allowed</color>
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>If players are in tenpai at the end of the round, it will still be valid even if they cannot go out because the hand is worth nothing.
30-0163:
<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>If you use the 2-han minimum rule, you can go out with a Seven Pairs</color>

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>No riichi ippatsu is allowed for the 2-han minimum rule!
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>If there are five or more bonus sticks on the table, you must have at least a 2-han hand to go out. (In this case, a dora does not
　　count as 1 han.)
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow>For example:
　　　(YES!): Only All simples, only Tsumo, Riichi Ippatsu, Tsumo-Dora 1, etc. 
　　　(NOPE!): Seven Pairs, All Simples + No-Points Hand + Dora, etc.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Calculating points
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Round to the nearest 100
　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Everyone's points will be rounded to the nearest 100 when calculating the final score.

30-0206:
<symbol=case_file_head>How to Concoct an Extract
　　You can make your own extracts by opening your Items App and going to the
　　Valuables tab, then selecting which <color=red>recipe</color> you want.

30-0208:
<symbol=case_file_head>Mundane Materials for Modern Magic
　　There are many different ingredients that are used to create extracts.

　　Other ingredients are only sold in stores, and some are given to you as gifts.

　　the city or during a fight by pressing <symbol=button_left>/<symbol=button_up>/<symbol=button_right>. Items that are mapped to a
