30-0212:
<symbol=case_file_head>The Lone Wanderer of Virtual Kamurocho

　<symbol=case_file_subhead><color=striking>Kuro-nyan</color> is a mischievous digital thief that that preys on delicious player data.
　　* Kuro-nyan appears in both the Middle and Long courses.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>If you come in contact with Kuro-nyan, <color=striking>all your items will be taken away</color>.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> After stealing your items, Kuro-nyan will flee to another space on the board.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Encountering Kuro-nyan after chasing him down will trigger a battle sequence.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> If you win, you will reclaim your stolen items.
　　　Moreover, you may even gain a bonus along with your victory.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>On rare occasions, purple enemies will appear during battle. If you fail to
　　defeat them, a new Kuro-nyan will spawn somewhere on the board.
30-0214:
<symbol=case_file_head>Bow Down to the King of Koro-nyans!


　<symbol=case_file_subhead><color=striking>King Koro-nyan</color> is the leader of the Koro-nyan tribe, and governs them from his virtual cat-stle.
　　* King Koro-nyan appears in both the Middle and Long courses.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>If you come in contact with King Koro-nyan, a bonus event called <color=striking>Koro-nyan Mode</color> will be triggered (see next page for details).

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Furthermore, King Koro-nyan will even heal mortal wounds that you've received in battle.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>On rare occasions, golden enemies will appear during battle. Defeat them to cause King Koro-nyan to spawn somewhere on the board.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>If you manage to spot King Koro-nyan, make sure to chase him down!
30-0215:
<symbol=case_file_head>Get Ready for a Big Payout!

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>If you manage to come in contact with Koro-nyan, <color=striking>Koro-nyan Mode</color> will activate.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>During Koro-nyan Mode, every space will automatically turn into Koro-nyan Spaces.
　　Each Koro-nyan Space triggers a bonus challenge that deals out huge rewards upon completion.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Rolling the dice during Koro-nyan Mode also nets you items depending on the number you roll.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Koro-nyan Mode <color=striking>ends once you move three spaces</color>.

30-0219:
<symbol=case_file_head>Flex Those Networking Skills

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>As Yagami's <color=striking>reputation</color> grows, he will be able to access more Side Cases.

　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> This is achieved by <color=striking>deepening your relationships with the locals</color> and friends that Yagami makes around town.


　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Some of these locals will have a <color=striking>special icon</color> that signifies that the two of you can become <color=striking>friends</color>.

　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> In order to become friends, you'll have to <color=striking>max out their Friendship Meter</color>.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Solving their issues and listening to their concerns will steadily fill up their Friendship Meter.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> When you want to see a friend but they're not around, try coming back and visiting them some other time.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead>Some clients will show up around town and become your friend only after solving their requests.
30-0221:
<symbol=case_file_head>During your VR adventure, you will engage in a variety of Battle Missions, each with their own unique set of rules.
　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Every Battle Mission has a <color=striking>time limit.</color>
　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> If you don't meet the conditions within the given time limit, you will fail the mission regardless of your remaining health.


<symbol=case_file_head><color=striking>Types of Battle Missions</color>

　<symbol=case_file_subhead><color=striking>Locked Style Battle</color>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> A battle that restricts you to only one combat style.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> You will not be able to switch styles at any time during this battle.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead><color=striking>Dire Battle</color>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> A battle where every enemy attack inflicts a mortal wound.
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> Mortal wounds can be healed if you encounter King Koro-nyan.

　<symbol=case_file_subhead><color=striking>Drone Battle</color>
　　<symbol=case_file_right_arrow> A battle that pits your drone against an enemy's to try and shoot them down.

32-0450: Security Camera Footage: Outside Club Amour (9:00 PM)
32-0451: The time was 9:00 on the night of the incident. The murder victim, Kume, is shown being forced into Club Amour by Hamura and four other Matsugane Family members. Kume's aniki, Murase, is also shown fleeing the vicinity.
32-0453: A camera installed at Club Amour's back entrance. It's broken, so it doesn't have any footage.
32-0455:
Kume's direct cause of death was brain trauma resulting from a stab wound through the eye. The murder weapon is thought to be an ice pick-shaped object. His body also showed signs of being assaulted while still alive.

Kume's time of death is thought to be between 2:00 and 3:00 AM. The amount of blood left at the body's location does not match the size of his wound. Therefore, it is thought that his body was relocated from the actual scene of the crime.
32-0457:
Taken around midnight on the night of the incident, this footage shows Hamura striking Seiya, a host at Stardust, and subsequently leaving the premises. Seiya witnessed Hamura entering Sauna Goten immediately afterward.

None of the clients at Goten had left the building until the first train arrived the following morning. Since Hamura was among these clients, it is highly likely that he stayed inside Goten until that time as well.
32-0459:
Many of the details surrounding Mashiba's death show striking similarities to that of his fellow victims, Kume and Kunimura. For example, Mashiba's direct cause of death was a stab wound through the eye that punctured all the way through to the brain. The murder weapon is also thought to be an ice pick-shaped object. Additionally, the amount of blood left at the location where the body was found does not match the size of the wound. Therefore, it is thought that
the body was relocated from the actual scene of the crime.
The victim neither carried a wallet nor a phone, and the actual place where the murder was carried out remains unknown.

32-0469:
Released by the ADDC in 2017, the miracle drug known as AD-9 was shown to be astoundingly effective against Alzheimer's during animal testing. It has since received international acclaim for its ability to treat a previously incurable disease.

The actual man behind the research was Professor Yoji Shono, but in order to garner more attention, Ryusuke Kido (a renowned scientist with a much more public persona) was listed as the author instead.

32-0475: A panoramic view of the hospital room where an elderly patient named Waku had stayed for two years. However, he suddenly disappeared from the hospital and was found buried in the mountains of Okutama three months later.
32-0477: Waku, an elderly ADDC patient, was diagnosed with major neurocognitive disorder after suffering through worsening stages of Alzheimer's disease; as such, he'd been hospitalized for two years. His body had already begun decomposing by the time it was found in the mountains of Okutama. Therefore, it can be assumed that he died during or immediately after the moment he went missing. Further details regarding the cause of death remains unknown, but the victim is believed to have died from suffocation.

A laundry cart used to collect bed sheets at the ADDC's hospital wing. Large enough to hide a person inside.

32-0481: Upon further investigation, the police found traces of the victim's bodily fluids in Okubo's truck bed. Subsequent DNA tests proved that the fluids belonged to Waku. Such evidence suggests that Okubo was behind the murder.
32-0483: Hashiki's cause of death was a cerebral contusion resulting from multiple blows to the head. The results of his bloodwork suggests that he was inebriated at the time he was killed. Move left or right to navigate around obstacles preemptively.
Avoiding these obstacles beforehand will eliminate the need to press any prompts.
34-1965: Be mindful of where your target is looking. If you enter the target's field of view, their Caution Gauge will rise, so keep your distance and stay out of sight as much as possible.
34-1966: Locate a spot to take cover when the target turns around. If there is a hiding place nearby, you can take cover there by pressing <symbol=button_maru>. There is no risk of getting spotted by the target while hiding for cover.
34-1967: Be careful not to get too close to your target. Your risk of being spotted increases substantially if you get too close, so make sure to keep a proper distance.
34-1968:
You can perform various EX Actions as the EX Gauge charges up.
EX Actions deal an incredible amount of damage, and come in handy when you're in a pinch.
34-1969:
Use recovery items whenever your health starts running low.
You can use items by either setting them as your shortcuts or navigating through the Items App.
34-1970:
If you want to improve your skills, go to the Pause Menu and open up the Skills App.
Powering up your skills will help you defeat powerful enemies.
Note that learning new skills requires SP.
34-1971:
Find the bomb hidden somewhere in the city before the timer runs out.
The bomber gave you a hint that should be at least somewhat related to a location in town.
34-1972:
Complete the objectives before the time limit reaches 0.
If you can't find the required object, it might be hiding behind something.
Try looking from a different angle to change up your perspective.
34-1973: Make sure you review the objectives before taking your picture, and be careful to avoid drawing your target's attention.
34-1974:
Your target might notice you if you get too close to them or move into their line of sight.
Keep your distance from the target and wait for the right moment to get that perfect shot.
34-1975:

"CAUTION" will display onscreen whenever an enemy targets your drone.

35-0003: Successfully pick the lock within the time limit. Lifting a pin too high may reset all the work you've done so far, so be sure to move the pins delicately.
35-0004: Matsugane is more frail than you. Prioritize helping him, especially if he gets surrounded.
35-0005: When battles are timed, you've got to make the most of your damage. Remember that the Tiger Style has single, high-powered attacks, while the Crane Style can deal with large enemy groups effectively. Moreover, EX Actions pause the timer, so use them liberally.
35-0006: Mafuyu isn't used to combat and will go down quickly. Prioritize helping her, especially when she's surrounded.
35-0007: Let your EX Gauge charge. EX Actions deal an incredible amount of damage and can be valuable in a pinch.
35-0008: Use a recovery item when your health runs low. You can set them to a shortcut or navigate to them through the Items app.
35-0009: Improve your skills through the Skills App by using SP. This should help give you an edge in battle.
35-0010: The Tiger Style is better suited to single, powerful foes. Unlike Crane, it can not only break enemy guards, but also makes you less likely to falter when blocked. It also contains some of your most powerful skills.
35-0011: The Tiger Style is better suited to single, powerful foes. To avoid Deadly Attacks, note that the enemy will be enveloped with an intense aura, and use wall kicks or EX Boosts to maximize your effectiveness against them.
